expectations.note: After clearing all preferences and restarting, the fresh Dot state had no song-info overlay.
I enabled show song info, restarted, played a fixture through the browser, and verified the overlay remained enabled and rendered.
I disabled show song info and restarted; the resulting Dot state had no overlay.

At 100% with genuinely long artist/title metadata, the captured screen displayed Flutter's Invalid argument(s): 20.0 error instead of a valid Dot hero; the overlay was not a clean, non-overlapping hero rendering.
At 150% with the same long metadata, the screenshot again showed the Invalid argument(s): 20.0 Flutter error and clipped text rather than a valid Dot hero.
My fresh normal-scale capture was an error screen, and the candidate's submitted normal screenshot used only short metadata and also visibly showed the Flutter error banner.
My fresh maximum-scale capture showed the Flutter error and clipped long text, while the candidate's submitted maximum screenshot contained only short metadata and the same error banner.
Normal- and maximum-scale verification bundles contained non-empty long artist/title semantics with non-zero bounds, corroborating that text was rendered in both states.

With ordinary undercover metadata at normal scale, the app remained navigable and showed the text, but the Dot hero was replaced by a visible Invalid argument(s): 20.0 Flutter error; the candidate's max-scale screenshot showed the same regression.

The app answered runtime probes and reported no overflow records, but repeated Dot/song-info exercise produced a visible Invalid argument(s): 20.0 Flutter error and a later restart temporarily lost the VM service.
